bible_refs.note: ζῇ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ is the lemma 2 Corinthians 13:4 (ἐσταυρώθη ἐξ ἀσθενείας, ἀλλὰ ζῇ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ); τὸ ἀσθενῆσαι answers ἐξ ἀσθενείας. Cited once inline at the lemma words.
τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ δύναμιν αὐτὸν τὸν Υἱόν echoes Χριστὸν θεοῦ δύναμιν (1 Corinthians 1:24).

choices.english: Yet He lives by the power of God
choices.why: γεμήν is the particle 'yet', not a form of γέμω ('be full'); the clause is the lemma 2 Corinthians 13:4.
rejected: he lives full of power from God

choices.english: has it of Himself and possesses it in His very being
choices.why: The power is His own by essence, not received from another.

choices.term: Θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν κατὰ φύσιν ὁ σαρκὶ παθὼν δι' ἡμᾶς
choices.english: the One who suffered in the flesh for us is God by nature
choices.why: One clause: the sufferer in the flesh is the subject, God by nature the predicate. It must not be attached to the next sentence about those who stumble.
rejected: Having suffered in the flesh for us, if they stumble

choices.why: Third-person imperative kept as an imperative.
Kept as the term used elsewhere in this book for God's saving plan in the flesh.

pass_a_gloss: For to God would befit and to [him] alone the being able to do all things; so as also to destroy the power of death itself, and to crown the body held fast by corruption with the grace of incorruption. Therefore he endured willingly to be weak briefly, at least according to the nature of the flesh; just as indeed he is said to hunger and to thirst and to toil/grow weary, and indeed also to die, on account of the economy; yet he lives from the power of God, and not having received from another the being able to do all things, but having [it] from his own home and existing-in [it] essentially; for God by nature is the one having suffered in flesh for us. Therefore if they are scandalized on account of the cross, let them marvel on account of the resurrection; and even if he should be said to live from the power of God, none the less you will understand the power of God [to be] the Son himself. [page number 17]
pass_b_english: For it befits God alone to be able to do all things, so as even to destroy the power of death itself, and to crown the body held fast by corruption with the grace of incorruption. So He willingly endured being weak for a little while, as far as the nature of the flesh is concerned, just as He is indeed said to have hungered (Matthew 4:2), to have thirsted (John 19:28), and to have grown weary (John 4:6), and even to have died, for the sake of the economy.

Yet He lives by the power of God (2 Corinthians 13:4). He did not receive the power to do all things from another, but has it of Himself and possesses it in His very being; for the One who suffered in the flesh for us is God by nature. So if they stumble over the cross, let them marvel at the resurrection. And even if He is said to live by the power of God, you will none the less understand the power of God to be the Son Himself (1 Corinthians 1:24).
source_text:
Θεῷ γὰρ ἂν πρέποι καὶ μόνῳ τὸ δύνασθαι πάντα δρᾶν· ὡς καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ θανάτου
καταλῦσαι τὸ κράτος, καὶ τὸ τῇ φθορᾷ κάτοχον σῶμα τῇ τῆς ἀφθαρσίας στεφανῶσαι
χάριτι. οὐκοῦν ὑπέμεινεν ἑκὼν τὸ ἀσθενῆσαι βραχὺ κατά γε τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς φύσιν·
καθάπερ ἀμέλει πεινῆσαί τε καὶ διψῆσαι καὶ κοπιάσαι λέγεται, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀποθανεῖν
διὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν· ζῇ γεμὴν ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ, καὶ οὐ παρ' ἑτέρου τὸ πάντα δύνασθαι
λαβὼν, ἀλλ' οἴκοθεν ἔχων καὶ οὐσιωδῶς ἐνυπάρχων· Θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν κατὰ φύσιν ὁ
σαρκὶ παθὼν δι' ἡμᾶς· Οὐκοῦν εἰ σκανδαλίζονται διὰ τὸν σταυρὸν, θαυμαζέτωσαν διὰ
τὴν ἀνάστασιν· κἂν εἰ λέγοιτο ζῆν ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ, οὐδὲν ἧττον νοήσεις τὴν τοῦ
Θεοῦ δύναμιν αὐτὸν τὸν Υἱόν.

review_notes: The u05-open source block is the whole of Unit 5 (it begins at Θεῷ γὰρ ἂν πρέποι and ends at αὐτὸν τὸν Υἱόν). The f2c_u05_rem trio re-split the same Greek and was parked on 2026-10-23 (see the book SESSION_HANDOFF.md), so this section is the only reader copy of Unit 5.

Θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν κατὰ φύσιν ὁ σαρκὶ παθὼν δι' ἡμᾶς is one clause: 'the One who suffered in the flesh for us is God by nature.' The parked u05-rem rows split it across a row break; that problem no longer reaches readers.
οἴκοθεν ἔχων καὶ οὐσιωδῶς ἐνυπάρχων: 'has it of Himself and possesses it in His very being' (the power is His own by essence, not received).

Possible allusions not cited inline: τοῦ θανάτου καταλῦσαι τὸ κράτος may echo Hebrews 2:14 (τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου); φθορά / ἀφθαρσία may echo 1 Corinthians 15:42, 53; σκανδαλίζονται διὰ τὸν σταυρόν may echo 1 Corinthians 1:23 or Galatians 5:11; ὁ σαρκὶ παθών may echo 1 Peter 4:1.
οἰκονομία is kept as 'the economy', the term used elsewhere in this book for God's saving plan in the flesh.
The trailing page number 17 is omitted. The source has no lacuna.
Divine pronouns are capitalised for clarity.
